$comment: How Semiont's worker cuts a text into chunks, as every implementation of that worker must cut it. The worker cuts a text into the pieces it sends a model one at a time, and where the next cut starts is what a job's cursor records, so two implementations of it that cut differently cannot take up each other's work. The cutting is that worker's own choice: no SDK has it, and a worker of another kind cuts a text as it likes. TypeScript (packages/core: estimateTokens, cutChunk, chunkText) runs every case and fails on a difference; an implementation of the worker in another language runs the same file. THE RULE. Every offset and every length here counts Unicode code points: `at` and `next`, a text's length, the 4 x chunkSize of a window and the 4 x overlap. A text's `estimatedTokens` is its length in code points divided by four, rounded up. A `chunking` is two numbers of tokens, `chunkSize` and `overlap`; `defaults` is the chunking used when none is given. A cut made at the offset `at` takes a `piece` of the text and says where the `next` cut starts. Its window ends at `at` + 4 x chunkSize, or at the end of the text if that comes first. When the window ends where the text does, the cut is there. Otherwise the cut is moved back to a boundary: the first of these three kinds that has one starting at or before the window's end and after the window's middle, which is `at` + 2 x chunkSize (after it, not at it). A blank line, the last "\n\n": the cut is where it starts. Else the end of a sentence, the last full stop followed by a space: the cut is after the full stop. Else the last space (U+0020 only): the cut is where it is. With none of them, the cut is at the window's end. A boundary that starts exactly at the window's end counts, so a piece cut after a full stop there is one code point longer than the window. The `piece` is the text from `at` to the cut, with the white space at both its ends removed. `next` is the length of the text when the cut is at its end; otherwise it is the cut less 4 x overlap, unless that is not after `at`, when it is the cut itself. A text's `chunks` are: none, for the empty text; the text itself, whole and untrimmed, when its estimatedTokens is no more than chunkSize; otherwise the pieces of the cuts made from 0, each at the `next` of the one before, until a cut's `next` is the length of the text, leaving out every piece that is empty. READING A CASE. Every case states `text`, its `estimatedTokens`, a `chunking`, the `chunks` of the text under it, and `cuts`: each a cut of the text under that chunking, made on its own at `at`, with the `piece` and `next` it answers. In every case the cuts are the walk from 0. White space is what Unicode gives the White_Space property; no case rests on U+0085 or U+FEFF, about which the trimming an implementation is born with disagrees. What an offset counts is held by a table of its own, specs/src/text/offset-cases.json; some texts here have a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, which is one code point and two UTF-16 code units, so that a count of code units fails them. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: the empty text has no tokens, no chunks, and nothing to cut
a text within one chunk is that chunk, whole and untrimmed; a cut of the same text trims it, and ends the walk
twenty characters are five tokens, exactly a chunk of five: still one chunk
one character more is six tokens, rounded up, and two chunks: with no boundary the cut is at the window's end, and the next starts an overlap of four characters back

a blank line after the middle of the window is where the cut goes, though a sentence end and a space lie nearer the window's end; the later cuts find that blank line behind their middle and take a sentence end, then a space
cases.text:
Alpha beta.

Gamma. Delta epsilon zeta.

cases.why: a blank line before the middle of the window does not count: the cut goes after the full stop of the last sentence end, and the piece keeps the full stop
cases.text:
Intro.

One two. Three four five six.

cases.why: a sentence end before the middle of the window does not count either: the cut goes at the last space
cases.text: One. Two three four five six seven.

cases.why: a space before the middle does not count, and one newline is neither a blank line nor a space: the cut is at the window's end, inside a word
a boundary exactly at the middle of the window is not after it: the blank line at 10 is passed over
a sentence end whose full stop is exactly at the window's end counts: the cut is after it, at 21, and the piece is 21 characters
a blank line that starts inside the window and ends outside it counts: the cut is at 19, where it starts, so the next cut starts at 15 and not at 16
an overlap that would put the next cut back where this one started is not taken: the cut at the space at 12, less an overlap of twelve characters, is 0, so the next cut starts at 12
a piece that is all white space is empty once trimmed: the cut is still made and the walk goes on from its `next`, but it is no chunk; with no overlap each cut starts where the last one ended

an ideographic space (U+3000) is white space and is trimmed from the end of a piece, but it is not a space to cut at: a text with no U+0020 is cut at the window's end; and twelve characters of three bytes each are three tokens, not nine
cases.text: 世界你好世界你　好世界你

cases.why: a combining mark is a code point of its own: an e and the acute accent after it (U+0301) are two, so this text is five code points and two tokens where the same word with a single accented letter would be four and one

a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is one code point: four of them, fifteen letters and a space are twenty code points and five tokens, so the text is one chunk, whole and untrimmed; a count of UTF-16 code units makes them twenty-four and six tokens, and cuts the text

a window of twenty code points that ends just after such a character takes the whole of it, since a cut is between two code points and never inside one; and the last cut's `next` is the text's twenty-six code points

a walk through a text with three such characters: the blank line is at 13 and the first cut's `next` is 9, the sentence ends at 22, the last space is at 39, and every one of them is a count of code points, as are the window's twenty and its middle
cases.text:
🎉 Alpha beta.

𝑥 Gamma. Delta 😀 epsilon zeta.

cases.why: a sentence end exactly at the middle of the window is not after it either: the full stop at 10 is passed over, and the cut is at the last space, 17
nor is a space exactly at the middle of the window: the space at 10 is passed over, and with no other boundary the cut is at the window's end, 20
